To: support@clockpoint.example
Replying to: m01
Cc: kevin.mutua@tausifreight.example
Subject: Re: [CP-48213] Overtime coding issue on night shifts

Dear Faith,

Thank you for picking this up. I've copied my colleague Kevin Mutua, our payroll officer, who will test whatever fix or workaround you suggest. Here are the details you asked for:

1. Terminal model and firmware
Four BX-300 terminals at our Embakasi depot. They auto-updated from 4.1.8 to 4.2.1 on the night of 27 October. Our two BX-300s at Mombasa Road are still on 4.1.8 because they were offline that week. That site's day shift exports correctly.

2. Shift template
NIGHT-8, 22:00 to 06:00.

3. Example
Employee ID T-0417. Clocked in 21:54 on 30 October and out 06:07 on 31 October.
Export showed: 2.1 hrs REG on 30 October and 6.1 hrs OT15 on 31 October.
Expected: 8.0 hrs REG plus 0.2 hrs OT15 on a single line. Our payroll rounds to the nearest tenth of an hour, so the 8 h 13 min total is 8.2 hrs, and only the 13 minutes outside the scheduled shift should be OT15.
Since the update, any shift that crosses midnight is split into two lines, and the after-midnight portion is coded OT15 instead of REG. This affects 38 night staff. Our draft October overtime came out about KES 212,000 too high, and we have had to correct it by hand from the raw punches.

4. Export profile
Payroll CSV v2.

5. When we noticed
5 November, while reviewing the draft October overtime. The problem appears to start from around 28 October, the first shifts after the update.

The 4.2.1 release notes promised improved midnight rollover handling. In our case it has done the opposite.

Our payroll inputs close on Friday 20 November, so we need either a fix or a clear workaround before then. We cannot keep correcting this manually every month.

I also need a plain answer on one question. Can our IT team safely roll the four Embakasi terminals back to 4.1.8 without losing any punch data, including anything held in the offline buffer? If it is safe, please send the correct procedure. If it isn't, please tell us what we should do instead. Should we also switch off auto-update on the Mombasa Road terminals for now?

Kind regards,
Njeri Mwangi
HR Manager, Tausi Freight
